newsitem.title: ITALY: SAI names Caruso chairman, premiums rise.
newsitem.headline: SAI names Caruso chairman, premiums rise.

text.p: Italy's largest car insurer Societa' Assicuratrice Industriale (SAI) announced that it had appointed Carmelo Caruso as its new chairman, while the group also added three new directors to its board.

The new three were Carlo Di Giacomo, Jonella Ligresti and Didier Pfeiffer, a SAI statement said. The new appointments replace ex-chairman Salvatore Ligresti, former managing director Fausto Rapisardo and Jean-Jacques Bonnaud.

SAI confirmed in late November that Ligresti and Rapisardo were resigning after Italian insurance watchdog Isvap had demanded that the two step down when they were found guilty of corruption charges relating to bribes paid by SAI to win an insurance contract from state energy group ENI.
The board also announced that premium income of the group for the first nine months of 1996 (January to September) rose 9.3 percent to 2.530 trillion lire.
In direct premiums, non-life business rose 9.2 percent to 2.083 trillion lire, and life business by 10.9 billion to 345 billion lire. Management costs rose only 2.6 percent, the group statement said.
